quests.title: What's It Doing in Cairnryan?
quests.summary: A resident of Aberdeen is planning a trip and wants a straight answer on the weather in Cairnryan.

steps.line: The weather? Oh, it's four seasons before lunch. Tell them to bring a coat and a sense of humour.
A coat and a sense of humour. I'll take both. That's the most useful forecast I've had all year.

start.ask: Aye, I'm thinking of a day trip to Cairnryan but I don't trust the forecast. Would you go and look at the sky for me?
start.accept: Look up. Report honestly. I'll dress accordingly.

quests.title: A Parcel for Fort William
quests.summary: Carry a brown-paper parcel to a relative in Fort William, then bring word back to Cairnryan.

steps.text: Take the parcel to Fort William.
steps.line: Oh, from Cairnryan? That'll be my sister's doing. A cardigan, again. Tell her I'm wearing the last one.

steps.text: Take the word back to Cairnryan.
steps.line: Oh, you've been! And she's wearing it? Well. That's me told, and a tea owed to you.

start.ask: Aye, would you do me a kindness? There's a parcel here for my sister in Fort William. It's only a cardigan and a lot of string.
start.accept: Marvellous. Mind the string, it's load-bearing.

quests.title: An Overdue Book
quests.summary: Return a library book that has wandered a long way, and tell the owner in Edinburgh it has gone home.

steps.line: Eleven years! We'd given it up for the Great Fire. There's no fine, but there is a look.

steps.text: Tell Edinburgh it has gone back.
steps.line: Gone back, and no fine? I'll leave the house with my head up. Here, for your trouble.

start.ask: Aye, this book is eleven years overdue and I've gone off the idea of walking it back. Could you take it to Inverness?
start.accept: Say it's from a friend. Say it was lost in a flood. Say anything.

quests.title: Seeds for Lerwick
quests.summary: A resident of Fort William has saved seed for a gardener in Lerwick. Take it over and bring back the news.

steps.line: Ah, her beans! I've been waiting all winter. Tell her I've a bed ready and a very smug cat.

steps.text: Take the thanks back to Fort William.
steps.line: Pleased as punch, was she? Good. Now I'll not have to carry them myself next year.

start.ask: Aye, I've saved a twist of seed for a fellow gardener in Lerwick. It's no weight at all. Would you carry it?
start.accept: Keep it dry. They're the best beans in the county, and I'll hear nothing against them.
